html:
Adulis was the port of the kingdom of Aksum on the Red Sea coast of what is now Eritrea, flourishing from about the 1st to the 7th century.

A Greek guide for merchants, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, names it as a market for ivory, tortoiseshell and rhinoceros horn, and ships from Egypt, Arabia and India called there. Through it came the goods, ideas and coins that tied Aksum to the Roman world, and probably the Christian faith too.

The 6th century traveller Cosmas copied a royal inscription he saw there. The port declined as Aksum weakened and Muslim powers took over the Red Sea trade, and its role passed later to Massawa nearby. Its ruins are still being dug.
sum: Adulis was the port of the kingdom of Aksum on the Red Sea coast of what is now Eritrea, flourishing from about the 1st to the 7th century.
